analysis.logline: At his own promotion party, a husband publicly throws out the wife who has quietly carried him, and her calm last instruction tells the room that his pride rests on something she controls.
analysis.tone: Family-friendly but cutting domestic drama: loud party cruelty on one side, held-back dignity on the other, ending on a half-laugh that has lost its confidence.

spine.act: Act I: The party and the expulsion
spine.note: Show a man's arrogance, a woman's patience, and the moment she accepts being sent away in front of everyone, leaving him one sentence he cannot ignore.

scenes.why: The audience watches a man humiliate his wife in front of twenty guests, and the instant she leaves with her father's pen and one calm sentence, his confidence cracks: the whole series turns on that sentence.
scenes.camera_approach: Wide at the party to place all three and the guests, then alternating close-ups that tighten as Richard grows louder and Esther grows quieter; an insert on the pen for the object that defines her; end tight on Richard's thumb stopping on the watch.

events.text: establishing view of INT. KALIO DUPLEX, PETER ODILI ROAD, PORT HARCOURT. NIGHT
Rain hammers the windows.
A promotion party is in full swing: twenty guests, a generator humming behind the wall, glasses clinking.
RICHARD KALIO (38), tight burgundy shirt, gold-rimmed sunglasses pushed up into his fade, holds a glass high and turns a heavy gold watch on his wrist.
At his elbow stands STEPHANIE SEKIBO (29), fuchsia dress, glossy bob, long French-tip nails.
ESTHER KALIO (33), in a plain sage-green wrapper and blouse, crosses the room with a tray of fried plantain and small chops, her head down.

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: Look at her! A primary school teacher, carrying plantain in my sitting room like a house girl. Esther, who asked you to serve my guests?

events.speaker: ESTHER
events.text: You did, Richard. This morning.

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: I asked you to stay in the kitchen. Not to stand where my colleagues can see you.

events.speaker: STEPHANIE
events.text: Richard, leave her. She is trying. Not everybody can be at this level.

segments.next_beat: Pack one bag. Go to your people in Warri. Go and sit in that falling house in Ekpan.

events.text: Esther's eyes go to Stephanie's hand on his sleeve, then back to Richard.
She sets the tray down on the side table, beside a brass-capped fountain pen lying on a folded exercise book.

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: Five years I have carried this woman. Her whole salary cannot fuel my generator for one month. Today they made me Deputy General Manager. Do you understand? I cannot stand on that stage with a woman who smells of chalk.
events.how: stepping closer, voice rising so every guest hears

events.speaker: ESTHER
events.text: What are you saying, Richard?

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: Pack one bag. Go to your people in Warri. Go and sit in that falling house in Ekpan.

events.speaker: ESTHER
events.text: In this rain? At night?

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: This roof is mine. Every plate, every light, every kobo in this house is my salary.
events.how: spreading his arms, smiling at the guests

events.text: He sweeps his hand across the side table.
The brass pen flies off and rolls across the tiles.

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: And take that market trinket with you. Seven years you carry it like a staff of office.

segments.heading: INT. KALIO DUPLEX, PETER ODILI ROAD, PORT HARCOURT. NIGHT
segments.location: kalio duplex peter odili road port harcourt night
segments.last_beat: His thumb stops turning the gold watch.

events.text: The pen stops against Stephanie's heel.
She smiles and does not move.
Esther crosses the floor, bends, picks it up, and wipes it slowly on her wrapper.
The room goes quiet.
Only the generator hums.

events.speaker: ESTHER
events.text: My father's pen is not a trinket.

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: Ladies and gentlemen, my wife, the poet!

events.speaker: ESTHER
events.text: You are sure, Richard? Before all these people?
events.how: lifting her bag from the chair, steady

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: I have never been surer. Without me, you will not eat.
Esther slides the pen into her pocket and opens the door.
Rain blows in across the tiles.

events.speaker: ESTHER
events.text: Tonight, when everyone has gone home, open your payslip. Read the bottom line. See whose name carries it.
The door closes.
Richard laughs, but it is only half a laugh.
His thumb stops turning the gold watch.
